walkthroughs.body_html:
Your heart fires itself.

The SAN (sinoatrial node) in the right atrium acts as a natural pacemaker — it sends an electrical wave that triggers each heartbeat.

If the SAN fails, doctors fit an artificial pacemaker — a small electrical device under the skin.

Mechanical valves replace leaky natural ones.

Stents prop open arteries narrowed by fatty plaques.

Statins lower blood cholesterol, reducing the chance of clots. For severe failure, a heart transplant may be needed.

Plasma: yellow liquid carrying CO₂, nutrients, wastes and hormones.

Red cells: full of haemoglobin that binds oxygen. White cells: fight pathogens. Platelets: cell fragments that clot wounds.

Arteries have thick muscular walls for high pressure; veins have valves to stop low-pressure backflow.

mcqs.q: Where is the body's natural pacemaker located?
options: Left ventricle
Right atrium (SAN)
Aorta
Brain stem

mcqs.q: Why do veins have valves but arteries do NOT?
options: Veins carry blood at LOW pressure so backflow is a risk
Veins are thicker so need them
Arteries always have valves too
Valves only exist in capillaries

mcqs.q: Do all arteries carry oxygenated blood?
options: All arteries carry oxygenated blood and all veins carry deoxygenated blood.
Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.
Arteries and veins both carry the same mixed blood through the body.
No — the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.

mcqs.q: How are signals transmitted across a synapse between two neurones?
options: Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.
Via neurotransmitter chemicals released from the presynaptic neurone, which bind receptors on the postsynaptic neurone.
The electrical signal jumps directly from one neurone to the next across the synaptic gap.
Neurones touch each other at synapses and pass current through direct contact.

mcqs.q: Why is a reflex action faster than a conscious response?
options: Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.
The brain decides reflexes faster than other actions because it skips thinking.
The signal does not need to be processed by the brain — it travels through a simpler reflex arc via the spinal cord.
Arteries and veins both carry the same mixed blood through the body.
